issues.legal_issue: A statutory pre-emption claim is not triggered unless the claimant deposits the full consideration stated in the transfer document together with the required surcharge, even when the claimant alleges that the stated consideration was inflated.
material_facts: The transfer document stated consideration of Rs. 5,21,000.
The pre-emption claimant alleged that the actual consideration was Rs. 2,50,000 and deposited Rs. 2,75,000, rather than the stated consideration with the surcharge.
The claimant sought to have the stated consideration examined before depositing the balance.

The Court held that the inquiry under Section 9 of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955, follows the deposit required by Section 8 and may address the stated consideration as well as additional sums proved by the transferee.
issues.conclusion: The full consideration stated in the transfer document, together with the required 10% surcharge, must be deposited to trigger the pre-emption right. A claimant may dispute the stated consideration, but that dispute does not excuse a short deposit; any excess may be refunded after inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8(1) and 9(1) of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955, read together, make the required deposit a precondition to exercise of the statutory right and to further inquiry. The Court applied the principle from Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh that pre-emption is a weak right to be strictly construed, and Gopal Sardar v. Karuna Sardar that the time requirement for exercising the right is sacrosanct. It also relied on Kedar Mishra v. State of Bihar concerning full deposit as a precondition, and on the plain-meaning approach to statutory construction in British India General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Captain Itbar Singh.

predicates.statutory_preemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks, under a statutory right of pre-emption, to be substituted for a purchaser of land.
predicates.full_stated_price_deposit_is_required: The governing statutory scheme requires the claimant to deposit the consideration stated in the transfer document together with a surcharge before the claim can proceed.
predicates.applicant_deposits_less_than_stated_pric: The claimant deposits less than the stated consideration and required surcharge, including where the claimant alleges that the stated price is inflated.

issues.definition: When a statutory pre-emption claimant deposits less than the stated price and required surcharge, the right is not triggered if full deposit is a prerequisite.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot extend the time for exercising a statutory pre-emption right by depositing the balance consideration after the prescribed period has expired.
material_facts: The claimant filed the pre-emption application with a deposit below the consideration stated in the transfer document and the required surcharge.
The appellate court directed the claimant to deposit the balance, but the claimant challenged that direction and did not complete the deposit within the prescribed period.
The Court had held that the statutory time for exercising the right could not be extended under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
The Court distinguished a case in which the required full deposit is completed within the period for exercising the right.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not be granted further time to deposit the balance after the prescribed period; the full deposit and the time for exercising the right are both mandatory.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 8(1) of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955, the right is exercised by making the required deposit within the prescribed period. Gopal Sardar v. Karuna Sardar holds that the time requirement cannot be extended through Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963. The Court held that the required amount and the prescribed period go hand in hand, while noting that a balance deposit made within the prescribed period may present a different situation.

predicates.statutory_preemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks, under a statutory right of pre-emption, to be substituted for a purchaser of land.
predicates.prescribed_claim_period_has_expired: The period fixed for exercising the statutory pre-emption right has ended.
predicates.full_required_deposit_was_not_made_withi: The claimant did not deposit the full required consideration and surcharge before the period for exercising the right ended.

issues.definition: If the prescribed period ends before the full required deposit is made in a statutory pre-emption proceeding, a later deposit cannot validate the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A deposit made by a pre-emption claimant must be returned if the claimant does not obtain the pre-emption right.
material_facts: The claimant had deposited money toward the pre-emption claim.
The claim did not succeed because the required deposit was not made within the prescribed period.
The Court stated that neither the purchaser nor the State could appropriate the deposited sum and directed its return, together with any interest earned if held in an interest-bearing deposit.
issues.conclusion: The claimant is entitled to the return of the deposited amount and any interest earned on it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reasoned that where the pre-emption right is not obtained, the purchaser cannot appropriate the claimant's deposit and the State should not retain it; the deposit must therefore be refunded. The Court directed return of any interest earned if the money had been kept in an interest-bearing deposit.

predicates.statutory_preemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks, under a statutory right of pre-emption, to be substituted for a purchaser of land.
predicates.claimant_deposit_is_held: Money deposited by the claimant toward the pre-emption claim remains held after the claim is decided.
predicates.claimant_does_not_obtain_preemption_righ: The claimant does not obtain the right to be substituted for the purchaser.

issues.definition: When a claimant's deposit remains held after the claimant fails to obtain pre-emption, the deposit and any interest earned are returned to the claimant.
